hook.text: A slightly taller giraffe eats more leaves. It survives longer and has more offspring. Nature just selected.

buildup.text: Darwin's natural selection works through variation, inheritance, and differential survival and reproduction.

discovery.text: Traits that improve survival in a given environment become more common in the population over generations.

twist.text: Selection has no goal or direction. It simply favors what works right now — not what's best or most complex.

climax.text: Natural selection is the engine of evolution. It shaped every primate body and brain, including yours.

punchline.text: Evolution doesn't plan. It just keeps what works.

quiz.question: How does natural selection work?
options: Organisms choose to evolve better traits
Traits aiding survival become more common over generations
Only the strongest survive regardless of traits

details.summary: Natural selection is the mechanism of evolution — individuals with traits better suited to their environment survive and reproduce more successfully, passing those traits to offspring. Over generations, this process produces adaptation, creating the fit between organisms and their environments.
details.whyItMatters: Natural selection is the foundation of evolutionary biology and the mechanism that shaped every aspect of human biology. Understanding it is essential for grasping how we became the species we are and how we continue to evolve today.
takeaways: Natural selection favors traits that increase survival and reproduction
It produces adaptation through differential reproductive success
It operates on inherited variation within populations over generations

faq.question: Does natural selection mean survival of the fittest?
faq.answer: Fitness in evolutionary terms means reproductive success, not physical strength. The fittest organism is the one that leaves the most viable offspring. Cooperation, camouflage, and parental care can be as fit as strength or speed. The phrase oversimplifies a nuanced process.

faq.question: Is natural selection still operating on humans?
faq.answer: Yes, though cultural buffering has changed its force. Differential reproduction still occurs — some people have more children than others. Medical technology, diet, lifestyle, and mate choice all interact with natural selection. Human evolution has not stopped; it has been altered by culture.
